> **Building up or building out**
> 
> Cities that grow face a choice that sounds technical but is deeply political: whether to expand outwards or to build more densely within existing boundaries.
> 
> Outward expansion is popular with residents because it delivers what many people say they want — a house with a garden. It is also, in the short term, cheap: land at the edge costs far less than land in the centre. The costs appear later. Roads, water pipes, schools and bus routes must be extended, and the number of households sharing each kilometre of infrastructure is low. Studies in several countries have found that the long-term public cost per household in low-density suburbs is roughly twice that in denser districts.
> 
> Density has the opposite profile. Construction is expensive and existing residents frequently oppose it, but each new home is served by infrastructure that already exists. Denser areas also support public transport, which requires a minimum number of passengers per stop to be viable.
> 
> The political difficulty is that the beneficiaries of density are diffuse and often not yet resident, while those who bear the immediate costs — noise, construction, changed views — live there now and vote. This asymmetry, rather than any technical obstacle, explains much of why cities continue to expand outwards even where the arguments point the other way.

ii. A choice with political consequences

iv. Why the better option is hard to deliver
v. The advantages and difficulties of density

writing.de_tom_tat: Task 2, ≥250 từ: Governments should build more housing in city centres vs. develop new towns outside cities. Discuss both views.
writing.bai_mau:
As urban populations continue to expand, governments must decide whether to increase housing density within existing city centres or to develop entirely new settlements beyond the urban boundary. Both strategies have significant merits, and the appropriate choice depends largely on local circumstances.

Building within city centres has obvious practical advantages. Residents can reach their workplaces, schools and hospitals without long journeys, which reduces both traffic congestion and carbon emissions. Existing infrastructure — water, electricity and public transport — is already in place, so the cost per household is comparatively low. However, this approach has clear limits. Central land is scarce and extremely expensive, and higher density can result in overcrowding, loss of green space and pressure on services that were designed for a smaller population.

Developing new towns, by contrast, allows planners to start from a blank page. Housing can be built at lower cost, with adequate parks, schools and cycle routes designed in from the outset. The principal drawback is dependency on transport links. If a new settlement is not connected to employment centres by reliable public transport, it risks becoming a commuter dormitory whose residents spend hours travelling each day.

In my opinion, neither strategy succeeds in isolation. The most effective policy combines moderate densification of central areas with well-connected satellite towns, linked by rail rather than road. What ultimately determines success is not the location of the housing but the quality of the connections between where people live and where they work.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Đề "Discuss both views" → bài trình bày cả hai chiến lược, mỗi bên có cả ưu và nhược điểm. Quan điểm riêng ở đoạn cuối là kết hợp cả hai, kèm điều kiện cụ thể (kết nối bằng đường sắt).
Mỗi đoạn thân bài xử lý một chiến lược trọn vẹn (ưu → nhược) thay vì tách ưu và nhược thành hai đoạn — cách này mạch lạc hơn. Từ nối: However · by contrast · The principal drawback · In my opinion.
urban boundary · increase housing density · infrastructure in place · cost per household · scarce · densification · satellite towns · commuter dormitory · from the outset.

Điều kiện loại 1 (If a new settlement is not connected… it risks becoming) · mệnh đề quan hệ với whose (whose residents spend hours) · cấu trúc nhấn mạnh (What ultimately determines success is…) · bị động (were designed for, can be built).

dang_hoc: Với đề so sánh hai phương án, mỗi đoạn thân bài xử lý một phương án trọn vẹn (cả ưu và nhược) — mạch lạc hơn là tách thành đoạn ưu và đoạn nhược.
Cấu trúc nhấn mạnh ở câu kết: What ultimately determines success is… — nâng điểm Grammatical Range.
"neither strategy succeeds in isolation" là cách nêu quan điểm kết hợp mà không nghe như trốn tránh.
Từ vựng quy hoạch đô thị đáng thuộc: density · infrastructure · satellite town · commuter · green space.
loi_thuong_gap: ❌ Chỉ trình bày một phương án → mất điểm Task Response.
❌ Nêu quan điểm "cả hai đều tốt" mà không có điều kiện cụ thể → nghe như tránh trả lời.
❌ Không có ví dụ hay hệ quả cụ thể → lập luận thiếu sức nặng.
❌ Viết quá 290 từ → hết thời gian cho Task 1, và lỗi ngữ pháp tăng.

speaking.de_tom_tat: Part 2 (2 phút) — Describe a place in your city you would change. Part 3 — Should cities grow upward or outward?

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Part 2 — Describe a place in your city you would change (2 phút)
cau_tra_loi.mau:
I'd like to talk about the area around my office, which is in the city centre.

It's a busy commercial district — offices, small shops, a lot of traffic. What strikes you immediately is that there's almost no green space. There are perhaps two small trees on the whole street, and nowhere to sit outside.

If I could change one thing, I'd pedestrianise part of it. At the moment the road takes up most of the width, even though very few people actually drive there — most of us arrive by motorbike or on foot.

I think the effect would be considerable. Cafés could put tables outside, people would walk more, and the air would be noticeably cleaner. Similar schemes have worked in other cities, so it isn't unrealistic.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Dàn ý Part 2: giới thiệu → tả hiện trạng → thay đổi mong muốn → hệ quả dự đoán. Bốn phần × 30 giây. Dùng điều kiện loại 2 xuyên suốt phần 3 và 4.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Part 3 — Should cities grow upward or outward?
cau_tra_loi.mau: Upward, in most cases. Building outward consumes farmland and makes people dependent on cars. Density isn't the problem in itself — badly designed density is. If tall buildings come with parks and good transport, they work perfectly well.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Trả lời dứt khoát trước, rồi tinh chỉnh ("Density isn't the problem in itself"). Đây là tư duy phản biện.
